novelty_rule: Accept a new source-supported rule, an untested rule-defined outcome branch, or an interaction whose timing/exception changes the ruling. Reject cosmetic wording, arbitrary number changes within a covered branch, and mechanical recombinations without a distinct timing/priority/exception issue.
authoring: Four sequential source-based reviews by the parent evaluator; these are not independent question-writer samples.
stopping_rule: After mapping all core procedural passages to questions, stop after two consecutive targeted passes add no meaningfully distinct, source-supported questions. This is working saturation within this source and criterion, not proof that no conceivable scenario remains.

accepted.why_distinct: Tests the source of the lap count and the optional USA learning exception; original Q18 assumes the final lap without defining the race length.
Original Q1 explicitly fixes a 6-Heat/3-Stress track; this tests the general source of setup quantities.
Original Q4 tests ordinary round order, not random initial grid assignment.
The reserve setup instruction is not requested in original Q1 or the spin-out question.
Adds an optional setup rule absent from all original questions.
Original Q2 establishes a two-position shift, but does not test the maximum or permission to buy additional shifts.
Tests the timing contrast with original Q8, where cooling can fund Boost during the same React step.
Original Q6 resolves one Stress only; this adds independent resolution and the distinction between committed and generated cards.
Tests whether base movement is optional or can be shortened; no original question asks this.
Combines blocked placement with the corner-speed calculation; original Q5 never checks a corner after blocking.
Tests the no-crossing branch; original corner questions all cross a line.
Adds the zero-cost boundary and distinguishes an empty Engine from an unaffordable cost.
Original Q12 tests insufficient Heat, not equality between the cost and remaining Heat.
Original Q11 assumes enough Heat for both corners and Q12 has a single corner; this tests which later corner fails after earlier payment.
Original Q12 tests the high-gear penalty only; this covers the other explicit penalty branch.
Tests 1st-gear allowance, additive Cooldown and optional use; original Q8 only uses 2nd-gear Cooldown 1.
Original Q7 lists both benefits, but does not ask whether they must be used together.
Adds the fewer-than-five branch and separates last-to-move eligibility from position after movement.
Original Q10 assumes legal qualification and never tests which positions qualify.
Adds a phase-order interaction that changes eligibility after Reveal & Move.
Tests whether simultaneous qualifying cars multiply the action; the original set never tests this.
Adds the interaction between optional Slipstream movement and the blocked-destination placement rule.
Original Q19 asks only about corners beyond the line; this contrasts corners on both sides in one turn.
Tests the nonfinal-lap branch of the exceptions in original Q19.
Original Q18 covers ranking and removal, not the condition for ending play for everyone.
Adds the source-defined distinction between two named lines; no advanced-play mechanics are requested.
Tests when the Cluttered Hand condition is evaluated relative to shifting, rather than the already-forced case in original Q17.

passes.focus: Unasked setup instructions, rule-defined boundary branches, Stress, movement, corner costs, cooling and Adrenaline.
Recheck phase order, movement exceptions, lap scope and when conditional failures are evaluated.
Try alternative card draws, gears, speeds, car counts, payments and final-lap outcomes against the expanded coverage map.
